newsitem.title: CHINA: SFC FIELDS COMPLAINTS ON BROKERAGE BRANCH CLOSURE.
newsitem.headline: SFC FIELDS COMPLAINTS ON BROKERAGE BRANCH CLOSURE.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said on Tuesday they received investors' complaints following the closure of a branch of Hing Shing Investment Company.
Known investor claims after the closure of Hing Shing's Kwun Tong branch and the disappearance of its manager were currently at about HK$14 million, they said in a joint statement.
"The SFC and the exchange are in close liaison with the owners of Hing Shing regarding the complaints," it said.
The company would invite clients trading through its Kwun Tong branch to register their claims, they said.

The owners of Hing Shing had demonstrated to the satisfaction of the SFC and the Exchange that it had liquid resources, in excess of HK$100 million, to meet its operational requirement and to cover potential claims, the statement said.
They would monitor the position closely to ensure that the company continued to have sufficient resources to meet its liabilities, it added. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
